title: Turn on Peer AI's lint rules, so sixteen standards stop being unenforced
goal: eslint.config.js uses peer-ai-eslint-config, so the sixteen rules nothing currently enforces (TS-02 to TS-09, REACT-01 to REACT-07, REACT-11) are actually checked. Then decide per rule whether it blocks now or is deferred against a named work item, rather than leaving the whole set reporting quietly.
acceptance: Given eslint.config.js, when lint runs, then peer-ai-eslint-config's settings are in effect ahead of the project's own settings
Given the repository, when peer-ai doctor runs, then it no longer reports that nothing enforces TS-02 to TS-09 or REACT-01 to REACT-07 and REACT-11
Given a violation of any newly enforced rule, when npm run verify runs, then it is reported rather than passing silently
Given a rule that cannot pass yet, when it is left non-blocking, then it is listed in standards.deferred with a reason, who decided it, and the work item that ends the deferral

reviews.summary: Pass with 1 medium open. No serious problem. FE-08 was the rule this branch was failing and now holds: a navigation failing after a successful save no longer reports the owner's figures as lost. The finding is that two of the four fixes are guarded by nothing — one provably cannot be guarded by a test, and the lint rule that would guard it was removed by this same change. ITEM-4 closes it.

Pass, 1 medium open. No serious problem, and the item strengthens the repository's posture: TS-02 and REACT-04 go from written-down to enforced here. The finding: the import path reads untrusted input and this change edits it, yet has a refusal test only for a merely-wrong file, none for input shaped to attack. Belongs with issue 106.

Pass. All four criteria hold and each was demonstrated rather than read: 15 peer-ai rules in the computed config, doctor's enforcers warning gone and replaced by two named deferrals with the owner's name, and an injected any plus non-null assertion produce errors that fail verify. One open finding carried from the security review: the untrusted import path this change edits has no abuse test.

Pass. DES-08 was being broken and is fixed — Rail's progressbar had no accessible name at all, because its label reached aria-valuetext, the value, rather than the name. A screen reader said "62% of food" with nothing saying what of. Proven by a test that fails when the attribute is removed. DES-13 computed from the tokens rather than deferred: all four tones clear 3:1 in both themes, worst 4.66:1.

Pass. DES-13 computed from the tokens rather than deferred: all four Rail tones clear 3:1 against their track in both themes, worst 4.66:1. Nothing visual changed — no colour, token, spacing or size is touched by any hunk, and the one added attribute is text. DES-07 is strengthened: the thing a coloured bar measures is now named, not just its percentage.

Pass with 2 high open, both recorded in full. Nothing audits dependencies on change or on a schedule, and 18 vulnerabilities are present (2 critical), all pre-existing and dev-only. eslint-plugin-jsx-a11y-x is a fork named one suffix from a better-known package, required by Peer AI's config, with no reason recorded in the tree. Re-checked at d00f246: the dependency diff is unchanged.

requiredReviews.reason: it changes code, at the mvp stage
it changes a screen, and the project has a design
it changes a dependency file or lockfile
its work item has acceptance criteria, which must all hold before it ships
